Yakuza 0 is a prequel to all the other Yakuza games and should be played first. It features a fantastic and serious main story about two Yakuza grunts between a rock and a hard place, with intrigues, betrayals and tragedy. It's one of my favourite game stories. It is interrupted by interesting and silly side stories about eccentricities of the Japanese society.
The beat 'em up gameplay is not my favourite part, but there are definitely some satisfying moves you can learn to power through it and become OP. There are plenty of minigames to keep it interesting.

It was first released on PS3/PS4 in 2015 and has been ported to PC in 2018. The port is well done, but there are some small improvements recommended, see PC Gaming Wiki: https://www.pcgamingwiki.com/wiki/Yakuza_0

The fact that SEGA sells all Yakuza games at such low prices on Steam (with and without a sale) is all the more reason to buy it!

One of the best games I ever played. It was a first of the game from this series I played.

I came to it expecting a mediocre game with fun side stories and wacky characters but it was so much more! The main plot is amazing and characters have depth, even if they are not the focus of the story (though not so much of progression, they are pretty much the same throughout).

I wasn't too fond of the fighting (it feels a bit repetitive) but it is really worth hanging on. I think I only scraped the surface with the fun side characters and doing about half of the extras plus the main story took me about 30 hours.

Only thing I have a gripe with is the disconnect between the gameplay and the characters. Not the silly ones where you beat 30 people and then go play slot cars or challenge some local boss in karaoke - more the parts where the protagonists are Yakuza that does not kill in cutscenes but bashing heads in the game or getting shot is no biggie.

I loved it though. If I don't think about it too hard and don't look for the flawed way it puts gameplay and narrative together I had a great time.

A lot of fun, drama and unpredictability. A truly emotional and honest game. Great gameplay, which will make you gladly kick ass all enemies. The plot and its turns will allow you to experience the routine of the real yakuza of that time. There is a place for almost everything.. heartbreaking scenes, scenes of revenge, relationships, and even humor. The game can surprise you even at the fiftieth hour. Each chapter is presented with something new. Whether it’s new gameplay mechanics or an unexpected course of events, in any case it will be worthy. Just a true masterpiece. I will definitely go through a few more times.

Yakuza 0 was my entry into the series, and after playing almost all of the other titles, I can without a doubt say this one is my favorite. It has the best story and the most side content/minigames (besides infinite wealth), the entire experience is so gripping. Of course this game is a completionist nightmare, but what a rewarding feeling is to platinum.

Yakuza 0 is a brilliant game.
Always wanted to sit down and finally give the Yakuza franchise a go, and I'm really glad I did.

The combat is hyper stylized and mechanically deep, combined with a brilliantly written crime drama that has a huge collection of memorable characters and moments.

Goro Majima and Kazuma Kiryu are excellent protagonists.
The world map is small but densely populated with super fun activities and side quests.

The fact that this game can jump from goofy, weird side quests to insanely fun street brawls to excellent dramatic character moments, all in a short amount of time, is very impressive.
Tonally, the switch between those elements shouldn't work at all, but it absolutely does here.

Having played other Yakuza games in the interim I’ve come to realize that’s essentially the standard for the entire series, which is awesome.

Yakuza 0 is fantastic and absolutely worth the time you invest in it.

In 10 days, this game will be delisted in favour of the Yakuza 0: Director's Cut edition, with a bloated file size, no mod support, no save file carry-over, a price hike that's twice as expensive, and 4 short extra story cutscenes that kill the pace of the existing story and assume you're not smart enough to work the story out. This update comes almost 10 years later to the game.
The original version of Yakuza 0 (this one!) is being delisted, becoming abandonware, in favour of their shiny new product of a fan favourite that they can sell for more money, to new and existing fans. A product that doesn't respect your ability to understand stories, a product made for you to give them more money for the same game.
I adore Yakuza 0, but I refuse to support the removal of the existing title in favour of the director's cut edition. I don't understand why both can't be purchaseable.

Yakuza 0 is the very first game from the series I played. Before that, I wasn't even sure if Yakuza is an RPG, shooter or a fighting game, so I approached it with no particular expectations and absolutely spoiler free.

And oh boy, what an experience it is! A gripping story, sizable and lively environment and so many side activities so I am pretty sure I still didn't find them all after playing the game for nearly 65 hours!

This game is a true sandbox - there is an interesting story which keeps its serious tone consistently, but the game allows you to do nearly anything for side activities. Singing a goofy karaoke song minutes after nearly beating somebody up to death? Of course!

I don't remember the last time I played a game giving me this much freedom and variety. For this reason alone I think this game is worth recommending to nearly anyone. Oh, and then there is a matter of price - since this game offers as much content as any AAA game, I think Y0 has a ridiculously low price! There are games twice as expensive which are not half as good as this game. You don't need to wait for a sale - you can grab this game right now and you definitely will not feel ripped off.

The game also has a local multiplayer in form of minigames (pool, bowling, dancing, darts) - nice little touch IMO.

5/5 Stars

The side quests and activities are hilarious as well. From delivering pizza, busting an underwear selling ring, tax fraud, running a girl's club, karaoke, and disco - this game has such a weird mess of things to do that just meshes so well with such a serious game.

Worth it at full price and an absolute steal on sale. The game is also on XBOX game pass if you own that as well!

A rollercoaster of emotion and endless entertainment. In the vast realm of gaming, there are few experiences as captivating and multifaceted as the one offered by Yakuza 0. The main storyline is a masterclass in storytelling, written with such finesse that it elevates the entire gaming experience. Also, what truly sets this game apart is its vast array of side content. It's a rollercoaster of emotions where laughter and heart-wrenching moments coexist seamlessly. The game's unique ability to elicit such diverse feelings is a rare and commendable feat. I can't recommend this game enough. It's a masterfully crafted experience that not only delivers an engaging main story with unparalleled character development but also provides an abundance of side content that ensures your adventure feels both vast and fulfilling. 10000000000000/10

It starts off slow and there's a lot of yapping in cutscenes but if you look past that, this is a brilliant game and a good introduction to the series if you're new. Shame on Sega for delisting this in favor of a modern, washed version.

Generally speaking I am mostly a virgin to actual japanese culture, and the only game I've played before that lets me walk around in Japan is persona 4 but I couldn't finish it unfortunately due to bugs. I was expecting an edgy, dark, mobster style game with graphics that would break my toaster pc, but as it turns out this is simultaneously a lighthearted and emotional story revolving around the development of three very well written and interesting main characters.

The supporting cast is also brilliant, and the side quests bring out much of the humor. It is a playful look at some serious issues facing Japan and the human condition itself. Ultimately, being the best Yakuza doesn't seem to mean being heartless in this game universe, rather, you need the biggest one. I got hooked by it, and the fighting is also quite satisfying, and the music is top tier. I really can't think of many bad things about it, other than walking around and minigames getting quite repetitive.

I think you will definitely enjoy this game if you put in the time.
